title: RAW UNREVIEWED: fixed grammatical suffix spelling can conceal spoken vowel harmony
summary: Retain a source-attested spelling architecture: a grammatical ending has an invariant written form although its pronunciation varies with linguistic context. The new input is a concrete official Ottoman spelling example, not a newly invented principle, a Turkish Voynich reading or an executed native test. Stem spelling, morphological parsing and lexical restoration must be separately paid.

design.human_rule: Write the same grammatical ending with its conventional spelling. Use known words and grammatical context when reading its pronunciation. Do not require one visible written symbol per pronounced sound.
not_a_complete_decoder: The source does not prove that stems never change when suffixes attach.
A reader needs lexical/morphological analyses and phonological environment, potentially preceding suffixes; an unknown stem alone is not a complete inverse.
No source morphological boundaries, phonemes, suffix identities or wordbook may be fitted retrospectively to each native form.
The modern teaching convention has no established1400native bridge. An early manuscript example still needs primary verification.
No role, English word meaning or sound is assigned to standalone dy, embedded dy, dal, daldy, or any other form. Their matching Latin letters are not a phonetic key.
design.positive_native_knowledge_used: Existing directed recurring parts and whole-form residuals motivate retaining a writing layer distinct from pronunciation. They neither identify a grammatical ending nor select Turkish. The already read complete f89v1 paragraph and oldDALfamilies supply no lexical anchor.
